_source: bench/bench_real_embeddings.py, GitHub Actions run 30604429019, ubuntu-24.04-arm (Cobalt 100, Neoverse N2), single core
_note: Committed so the headline table can be read without re-running CI. Raw console output alongside in real-embeddings.txt.

dataset.anisotropy_note: higher is more skewed, which is harder for uniform quantization; real embeddings are much harder than the Gaussian data a synthetic benchmark would use

results.note: fastest working FAISS int8, the baseline we quote
no SIMD, separate translation unit, CI asserts zero SIMD instructions

instruction_stack.note: the design change alone lands at 143.8 QPS, below the 231.2 of the FAISS index it replaces; symmetric quantization buys eligibility, not speed

pq_concession: PQ fast-scan is faster in absolute terms at every setting. It cannot enter the 0.97 to 0.99 recall band on this data, topping out at 0.787. If lower recall is acceptable, PQ is the right tool and this is not it.
